problems.note: Two pans with 3 pieces each (6 pieces total), 4 shaded. The marked answer 4/3 counts thirds, but 4/6 and 2/3 are the same share of the whole set (4 of 6 pieces = 2/3). So three choices are true in standard math (4/3, 4/6, 2/3), which breaks the one-right-answer rule. A child who reads 2/3 of all the pieces would be marked wrong. Fix by removing 4/6 and 2/3, or by asking explicitly how many thirds are shaded. Story card 6 uses the same per-piece counting convention, so the wording should match it.

Narration says 3 granola bars, but the picture is 3 × 🍫 (chocolate bar). Change the emoji to a granola-style bar or change the narration to chocolate bars so audio and picture agree. The picture also does not show the sharing, so the answer depends on the narration alone.

The question asks how many pieces are left (8 − 3 = 5). That is whole-number subtraction, not reading a fraction, so it drifts from the skill. Consider asking for the fraction that is left unshaded (5/8) or dropping the item.

Card 6 says 5 shaded pieces from 2 pans of 4 is 5/4, but it does not say why the bottom number is 4 and not 8 (each pan is one whole, so pieces are fourths). Add one sentence on this, since children may read it as 5/8. The same gap is behind the tap-6 ambiguity.
